definition: BigDL is a distributed deep learning framework for Apache Spark, created by Jason Dai at Intel.
details: BigDL has its source code hosted on GitHub.

explainer.lead: BigDL brings distributed deep learning to Apache Spark, so deep-learning work can run alongside Spark data processing. Created by Jason Dai at Intel, it is useful when a team wants to use a Spark cluster rather than build a separate deep-learning system.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team of people sorting a huge pile of information together. BigDL helps that same team also train a computer to recognize patterns, instead of sending the pile somewhere else. It works with Apache Spark, a tool for sharing large computing jobs across many computers.
tiers.practitioner: BigDL is applied when deep-learning workloads need to run within an Apache Spark environment. Engineering work therefore involves both the deep-learning job and the distributed Spark cluster running it. Its source code is hosted on GitHub.
tiers.paperLevel: BigDL is a distributed deep-learning framework built for Apache Spark, created by Jason Dai at Intel. Its defining feature is the integration of deep learning with Spark's distributed computing environment rather than a particular neural-network equation or architecture. The supplied information does not establish a specific originating paper or benchmark result.

explainer.example: A company with a large dataset already processed by Apache Spark can use BigDL to run a deep-learning job on its Spark cluster. This keeps the learning stage within the same distributed environment as the data-processing stage.

usedIn.name: Apache Spark
usedIn.detail: BigDL provides a way to run distributed deep-learning work in Spark-based computing environments.

usedIn.name: Distributed deep learning
usedIn.detail: It is used where deep-learning jobs need to be spread across a Spark cluster.

explainer.intuition: If your data and computing jobs already live in Apache Spark, BigDL lets deep learning happen in that same distributed setting. The central idea is to combine deep learning with Spark instead of treating them as separate systems.
howItWorks: Start with data and computing resources managed through Apache Spark.
Use BigDL to define the deep-learning work to be performed.
Run that work through BigDL's Spark-based distributed framework.
Use the resulting deep-learning computation within the broader Spark workflow.
explainer.whyItMatters: BigDL connects deep learning with an established distributed data-processing system. That can simplify workflows for organizations whose data infrastructure is already based on Spark.
misconceptions: BigDL is not Apache Spark itself; it is a deep-learning framework made for Spark.
It is not a neural-network architecture or a single trained model.
Jason Dai is its creator, while Intel is where he created it.
